tasks.title: Product direction: overview-first analyzer with a built-in Power Platform add-on
tasks.brief: Structra is a fully local JSON analyzer for everyone. The Power Platform tools (expressions, Parse JSON schema, Power Fx, flow actions) ship built in as an always-visible add-on for makers using canvas apps and cloud flows. Main job: understand an unknown payload in under a minute. Look: calm workbench.

subtasks.title: Overview replaces Stats and opens first after load (files up to 25 MB; bigger files open on the tree): plain-language headline, key figures, 'worth a look' findings with one-click jumps, biggest lists grouped by pattern, then the existing detail tables. Logic in core/insights.js

Guided first run: welcome dialog, paste anywhere with Ctrl+V on an empty tab, a 'try a sample' link under the drop area, and a one-time tip after the first document about the Power Platform expressions
First-run welcome dialog (shown once, reopen from the command palette as 'Welcome'): purpose, privacy, Power Platform add-on, light/dark choice, Try a sample / Open a file / Skip

Power Platform add-on prominent: the rail's Power Platform button opens the Expressions tab (it did nothing before), the Overview flags connector-shaped payloads, the Transform and Settings rail buttons now work too, and the rail highlight follows what is open

Power Automate expressions: source selector (action output, trigger body, loop item, custom), null-safe ?['k'] and ?[0], whole-action-output detection; checked against Microsoft docs, unit tested and verified in the browser
Parse JSON schema: nullable keys as type lists, nested objects and lists merged across rows, 'number' by default with an integer option, required toggle; unit tested
Power Fx: each column converted by its real type (Value, Boolean, DateValue, DateTimeValue, Text), quoted names, editable variable; unit tested
Flow actions tab: Select, Filter array, Apply to each, Compose and Condition as copyable action JSON; unit tested and verified in the browser
Committed fixture smoke test: npm run test:smoke (PW_CHANNEL=msedge to use the installed Edge); 30 fixtures x 6 views, fails on any page error or missing Overview headline

Node unit tests: npm test runs 47 tests (engine analysis, schema generation, expressions and paths, insights). The test runner now waits for async tests; before that an async failure could have printed ok

Large files, measured with tests/perf/large.js (Edge): the 37 MB file shows the Overview in 0.5 s (worst freeze 0.15 s) and the 88 MB file in 2.0 s (worst freeze 0.67 s, 210 MB heap). Overview now opens first up to 120 MB. Not built: a cancel button, and a worker for parsing (the earlier test found copying the data to a worker cost more than parsing it)

Engine duplicates removed: one _tableOf(ds) instead of 14 copies, CSV export reuses Structra.convert.generateCsv (it also handles nested values correctly). Fixed a bug found on the way: SQL find results broke the tree filter because it expected a Set but got a list. The JavaScript and DuckDB paths themselves stay: DuckDB is optional and loads on demand, so the JavaScript path is the fallback by design

Dialogs on the shared overlay base: shortcuts, typedef, diff, null finder, pivot, snippets and workspace now use StructraOverlay (open, close, Escape, backdrop, focus trap come from one place); about 35 old overlay, panel and header CSS rules removed. The smoke test opens and closes ten dialogs

tasks.title: One icon system (Lucide, ISC licence, bundled locally)
tasks.brief: About 70 inline SVGs were hand-copied across components (the close X alone appeared 9 times) plus glyph icons. Now every icon comes from the Lucide library (ISC licence) through one small wrapper, Structra.icons. The library loads from the jsDelivr CDN with a bundled copy as the offline fallback; only icon artwork is fetched, data processing stays local.

subtasks.title: Pick the library: Lucide (ISC, stroke icons that match the current Feather-style set, 1,500+ icons, per-icon SVG files)

API: svg(name, {size, cls, color, stroke}), has(name), hydrate(root) for <i data-icon> placeholders; color accepts theme token names so icons follow every theme
Replace inline SVGs in all components, header, rail, canvas header, overlays, index.html
Command palette: icon names instead of raw path strings
Replace glyph and emoji icons (play, check, times, swap arrows, status marks) with icons

Check every screen in dark and light; run the 30-fixture smoke test

Editor view: the status says only 'Invalid' (and Apply says 'Invalid JSON — cannot apply') with no line, column or reason, and no marker in the text; there is no line-number gutter, and the text font is larger than the Tree's, so the two views look like different apps
Editor view keeps the Tree toolbar (+All, -All, D1 to D3, Wrap, Filter, Find, Edit) although most do nothing in the Editor; the toolbar should change per view and Wrap should apply to the editor

After Apply in the Editor the tab keeps the name 'sample-data.json' with no 'edited' dot, so a maker cannot tell the file no longer matches what was opened; there is no Revert to original or Save as file

Editor Repair works well (single quotes, trailing comma, comment, True) but the repair message for hopeless input is jargon ('Unexpected end of json string at position 1'); also no diff of what was repaired

principles: Fresh rewrite: reuse V1 logic, but no backward-compatibility layers (no window.App shims). Everything lives under window.Structra.
V2 should end up better and different from V1, not a copy.
followUps: Session restore works (tabs, view, path, stored original). It only saves the stored copy once the page is idle, so a reload within a few seconds of opening a file restores an empty tab.
Fixture smoke test (30 small V1 fixtures, all six views each) passed with zero page errors after the redesign. It is run by hand through Playwright; task 10.8 turns it into a committed script.
Task 12 smoke run: 30 of 30 fixtures opened in all six views with zero page errors, and TypeScript generation checked on jsonobject.json.
Top-level null, false, 0 and empty string documents cannot be opened (jsonData doubles as the has-data flag). The app shows a clear message instead.
Large files (above 120 MB) open on the tree, and there is no cancel button. Parsing stays on the main thread because copying data to a worker cost more than parsing it.

Fixed after the light-mode pass: the side-by-side diff never highlighted changed lines (line numbers were never set); it now marks changed, removed and added lines by data path. The font-size token now matches the 14 px the app actually runs at.
